chapter: Armstrong, Parker and life inside the Basie band
title: Song pluggers and paying for radio time at the Hotel Lincoln
summary: Basie played tunes by Nick Kenny on coast-to-coast broadcasts, and shared the cost of air time with the hotel.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: In terms of the material you recorded, that was entirely up to the band? Or would the song pluggers telling you to record a certain song?

Well, he has done that, yeah. He has done that. But mostly the things we recorded in the early days were things with the band. Of course, after -- when we started playing the Hotel Lincoln and places like that, he started playing a lot of tunes that would be, you know, NBC, because we had the coast-to-coast hook-up. I remember Nick Kinn -- you know a writer named Nick Kinn?
He must be. Well, he used to do a lot of -- Basie used to play a lot of his songs on the air.
I guess he wrote -- I think he wrote a thing with Duke.
"Drop Me Off in Harlem," I think.
Did he write that with Duke?

Uh-huh. Then I know Basie used to do a lot of his songs and sometimes, you know, like we'd be on coast-to-coast hook-up and some things that he would suggest didn't please us, you know what I mean, because we'd want to swing, you know, and he'd play some funny kind of things. So we didn't know what was happening. But we found out, you know.
He'd be paid to play certain things.
Yeah, you know, then of course, he -- you know, he had to be in with the people and I found out that a lot of his air time, he had to pay half of it. Maybe the hotel

would pay for half and he had to pay for the other half. So I imagine he needed it, you know what I mean? Because, well, you know, by this time, he's got about 18 -- 17, 18 pieces. So he needed -- I guess he needed all the help he could get.
